messages.subject: plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace problems
parts:
Dear all,
I'm a very beginner user of geomorph package and of R in general.
In order to try plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace I prepared a tiny dataset with three species (aa, bb and cc) and 10 landmarks.
I have my tps file.
I load the geomorph and ape packages.

> mydata <-readland.tps("coo.tps", specID = c("ID"))
> Y <- gpagen(A = mydata, curves = NULL, surfaces = NULL, ProcD = TRUE, Proj = TRUE)
> print(Y$coords)

, , bb

             X            Y
1   0.08538000 -0.167831706
2   0.10131420 -0.151752474
3   0.09368636 -0.133347894
4   0.11413417  0.137330045
5   0.12302980  0.150902389
6   0.11284413  0.174970347
7  -0.48091821 -0.266406450
8  -0.07512289 -0.001332443
9  -0.49314564  0.264505124
10  0.41879809 -0.007036938

, , cc

             X            Y
1   0.10990727 -0.205949653
2   0.11929931 -0.186478034
3   0.10616423 -0.168931843
4   0.08223465  0.157777681
5   0.09805999  0.177332149
6   0.07837534  0.202831957
7  -0.48529001 -0.275687917
8  -0.07183562 -0.005524365
9  -0.42900484  0.293935450
10  0.39208967  0.010694575

, , aa

            X             Y
1   0.1103264 -0.1894024438
2   0.1133780 -0.1649145935
3   0.1022796 -0.1381219613
4   0.1033028  0.1505339653
5   0.1108817  0.1656029289
6   0.1020892  0.1883389563
7  -0.4617678 -0.2969464431
8  -0.1309913  0.0007347901
9  -0.4465918  0.3001817982
10  0.3970932 -0.0160069971

Then I have to prepare the tree:

> phy <- ape::read.tree(text = '(aa, (bb, cc));')
> str(phy)
List of 3
 $ edge     : int [1:4, 1:2] 4 4 5 5 1 5 2 3
 $ Nnode    : int 2
 $ tip.label: chr [1:3] "aa" "bb" "cc"
 - attr(*, "class")= chr "phylo"
 - attr(*, "order")= chr "cladewise"

> plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace(phy, Y$coords)
Error in edge[, 3] : indice fuori limite

"indice fuori limite" is for index out of the limit.
May you give me an advice? What's wrong?
Many thanks in advance.
Sara

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace problems
parts:
Your tree does not have branch lengths. That is one problem

Dean
